title: The column that stopped the stream
outcome: An analyst added a column to a busy silver table at midday; the stream reading it stopped and a concurrent write failed.

content.bookmark: A schema change ends every stream reading the table and conflicts with concurrent writes. Make schema changes on purpose, at a planned time, with streams set to restart.

check.prompt: A stream reads a Delta table. Someone adds a column to that table. What happens to the stream?
options: Nothing: new columns are picked up silently
It stops and must be restarted
It switches to reading in batch
check.why: Updating a table's schema terminates any stream reading it; the stream must be restarted.

check.prompt: An INSERT writes an INT value into a BIGINT column. What happens?
options: It succeeds by a safe cast
It fails with a type mismatch
check.why: Schema enforcement first tries a safe cast; an INT into a BIGINT column succeeds.

check.prompt: A write with mergeSchema adds a new column. Where does it go?
options: At the start of the table
check.why: Automatic schema evolution adds new columns at the end (or at the end of their struct), with their case preserved.

check.prompt: What lets you rename or drop a column without rewriting the data files?
check.why: Renaming and dropping columns without a rewrite need column mapping enabled on the table.

caseStudy.setting: A telecoms company (fictional) keeps call records in silver.calls. A continuous job streams silver.calls into a gold aggregate, and an hourly job MERGEs late corrections into silver.calls.

events.what: An analyst who owns a report runs ALTER TABLE silver.calls ADD COLUMNS (roaming_flag BOOLEAN) to prepare for a new field.
The gold stream stops. The hourly MERGE, running at the same moment, fails with DELTA_METADATA_CHANGED.
The continuous job restarts the stream and it carries on; the MERGE succeeds on its next run. The analyst asks why a harmless column caused two failures.

pipeline: silver.calls · Delta table, written by an hourly MERGE
Continuous job · streams silver.calls into gold
ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMNS · run by hand
tasks: Why did adding a column cause two failures?
How should schema changes be made on this table?

debrief.title: Why two failures
text: Adding a column is a metadata change. A schema update terminates any stream reading the table, so the gold stream stopped and needed a restart.
Metadata changes also conflict with concurrent writes. The MERGE had read the table before the change and failed its commit with DELTA_METADATA_CHANGED instead of writing against an outdated schema.

debrief.title: Why it recovered
text: The stream ran in a continuous job, which starts a new run after a failure. Designing streams to restart automatically is Databricks' production advice for exactly these stops.
The MERGE succeeded on its next run because the conflict was a one-off. Retrying is the documented answer to a concurrent-modification error.

debrief.title: Making schema changes safely
text: Schedule schema and property changes away from writes, and have them made by the table's owners, ideally through the same deployment process as the pipeline code.
Often no hand-run ALTER is needed: a write with mergeSchema or MERGE WITH SCHEMA EVOLUTION adds the column when data for it first arrives.

takeaway: A schema change terminates streams reading the table.
Metadata changes conflict with concurrent writes; retry them.
Plan schema changes; let streams restart automatically.
content.honesty: If you haven't changed the schema of a live Delta table, say so, and explain why it stops streams and conflicts with writes. If you have, describe how you scheduled it.

tasks: Who should decide when a shared table's schema changes?
What would you agree with report owners?

debrief.title: Who decides
text: The table's owner, as a planned change, not whoever needs the column first.

debrief.title: Agreement
text: Report owners request schema changes from the table owner, who schedules them with the pipeline.

sayIt.question: How do you manage changes to data that several teams depend on?
points: Give each shared table an owner.
Route changes through the owner.
Schedule changes so they don't disrupt running work.
Tell dependent teams in advance.
Review incidents to improve the process.

tasks: Was this an incident worth reporting?

debrief.title: Reporting
text: Yes, briefly: both failures recovered on their own within minutes, which shows the restart design worked; the cause still needs fixing.

debrief.title: Change
text: Agree who can change schemas on production tables and when.

sayIt.question: A small change caused a brief outage that fixed itself. How do you follow up?
points: Record it even though it recovered.
Find why a small change had an effect.
Note what worked, such as automatic recovery.
Fix the cause with a process or permission change.
Share the lesson with other teams.

tasks: What process change would you make?
How do you put it in place without blocking analysts?

debrief.title: Process
text: Schema changes on production tables go through the pipeline's deployment, at a planned time.

debrief.title: Not blocking
text: Give analysts a quick way to request a change, and let schema evolution on writes add columns when data arrives.

sayIt.question: How do you introduce a control without slowing teams down?
points: Explain the problem the control prevents.
Offer a fast, easy path for legitimate requests.
Automate where possible.
Measure whether it slows work.
Adjust based on feedback.

tasks: How would you make the change next time?
What should the stream and the MERGE be ready for?

debrief.title: Next time
text: Use MERGE WITH SCHEMA EVOLUTION in the hourly job, or schedule the ALTER between runs through the deployment process.

debrief.title: Readiness
text: Streams restart automatically; writers retry on concurrent-modification errors.

sayIt.question: Explain schema enforcement and evolution in Delta Lake.
points: Enforcement checks writes against the table's schema, trying safe casts first.
Evolution adds, reorders, renames and widens columns, explicitly with DDL or with DML options.
mergeSchema and WITH SCHEMA EVOLUTION add new columns at the end.
Rename and drop without rewriting need column mapping.
Schema changes stop streams reading the table and conflict with concurrent writes.
